Backend derives humanId = keccak256(abi.encode(nullifier)) and signs an    EIP-712 Attestation(humanId, userAddress, deadline) with the attestor key. 3. Human calls issueAgent() \u2014 VeriRegistrar verifies the attestation, enforces    the per-human cap, then mints an ENSv2 subname via the UserRegistry. 4. Scoped capabilities are granted as real EAC roles on the resolver \u2014 the    ENS protocol enforces what each agent may write, not Veri's own storage. 5. revokeCapability() strips the resolver role; the same write that previously    succeeded now reverts with an EAC error from ENS itself. \u2500\u2500 Trust assumption (stated openly) \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500 World ID ZK proofs are verified off-chain by the backend. The on-chain World ID verifier does not live on Sepolia; ENSv2 beta exists only on Sepolia. The trust assumption is: the attestor signing key is not compromised. params._registry: ENSv2 UserRegistry proxy for veri.eth (from SetupRegistry.s.sol).

eip712Domain().details: returns the fields and values that describe the domain separator used by this contract for EIP-712 signature.

grantCapability(string,bytes32).details: Token ID is resolved fresh here — do NOT cache it.

params._agentAddress: Agent's Sepolia address — receives the ENSv2 ERC-1155 token.
params.attestation: EIP-712 signature from `attestor` over                      Attestation(humanId, msg.sender, deadline).
params.capabilityIds: Capability IDs to grant on issuance (may be empty).
params.deadline: Unix timestamp after which the attestation is invalid.
params.label: Leaf label only — e.g. "scanner" → scanner.veri.eth.                      No dots. No parent. ASCII recommended.

returns.tokenId: ENSv2 token ID for the registered name (do not cache — mutable).

owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

renounceOwnership().details: Leaves the contract without owner. It will not be possible to call `onlyOwner` functions. Can only be called by the current owner. NOTE: Renouncing ownership will leave the contract without an owner, thereby disabling any functionality that is only available to the owner.

transferOwnership(address).details: Transfers ownership of the contract to a new account (`newOwner`). Can only be called by the current owner.

AGENT_ROLE_BITMAP().notice: Registry-level roles granted to the agent address on name registration.

CAP_SELF_DESCRIBE().notice: Agent may write its own `agent-context` text record.

CAP_SUBAGENT_ISSUE().notice: Agent may set a sub-registry — enabling it to issue its own sub-agents.

CAP_TRANSACT().notice: Off-chain signal: relying parties may transact with this agent.         No resolver role is granted — consumed entirely off-chain.

PARENT_NAME().notice: The parent name every agent is registered under.

attestor().notice: Address whose EIP-712 signatures authorise agent issuance.         This is the backend's signing key — keep it secret.

defaultResolver().notice: Default resolver for new names — PermissionedResolverImpl for veri.eth.         Set at deploy time; update with setDefaultResolver() if resolver changes.

grantCapability(string,bytes32).notice: Grant a capability to an already-issued agent.         Caller must be the human wallet that originally called issueAgent().

hasCapability(string,bytes32).notice: Returns true if the agent currently holds the given capability.

issueAgent(string,address,bytes32,bytes3.notice: Issue a new agent subname under veri.eth.

retireAgent(string).notice: Retire an agent from the Veri registry.         The ENSv2 name is NOT burned — the agent keeps its on-chain identity         and history. Retirement only removes the agent from Veri's registry,         decrements the human's agent count, and emits AgentRetired (which the         subgraph picks up to mark the agent inactive).         This also frees a slot so the human can issue a replacement agent.

revokeCapability(string,bytes32,string).notice: Revoke a capability from an agent.         Strips the corresponding EAC resolver role — subsequent writes by         the agent to that record will revert with an EAC error from ENS.         The agent keeps its name and history; only the right is removed.

setCapabilityConfig(bytes32,uint8,uint25.notice: Update the target/role/text-key config for a capability.         Call this after verifying the exact role constants in PermissionedResolverImpl.

setDefaultResolver(address).notice: Update the default resolver (if the veri.eth resolver is migrated).
